chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Uyayna, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the woman to wear while she is in Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'All clothes, except the two gloves, the burqa (veil), and silk.' I said, 'She can wear khazz (silk-like fabric)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'Supposing its warp is ibrisam (raw silk) and it is (also) silk?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as it is not purely silk, there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْخَزَّ: Khazz (a type of silk or silk-like fabric)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَةٌ: A woman in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What clothes are forbidden for a woman to wear while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on women's face veils (burqa) and gloves during Ihram is specific to these items, distinguishing it from the general prohibition on men wearing sewn garments. The ruling on silk emphasizes purity of material, permitting mixed fabrics like those containing ibrisam as long as they are not exclusively pure silk, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of leniency in mixed textiles. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the gender-specific distinctions in Ihram attire within Shia fiqh.
